name: Failed One-Concept Augmentation Localizes to an Antipodal Pair
statement: Let $K\subseteq Q_X$ be ample and $d\notin K$. Then $K\cup\{d\}$ is nonample if and only if there is a set $T\subseteq X$ with $|T|\ge2$ such that, for $h=d^{\oplus T}$, one has $h\in K$ and $(K\cup\{d\})\cap Q_T(d)=\{d,h\}$. Equivalently, the failed augmentation has a conditioning consisting of the two antipodes of a face of dimension at least two.
proof: The displayed antipodal pair is a nonample conditioning, proving sufficiency. Conversely, condition $K\cup\{d\}$ until reaching a conditioning-minimal nonample class $H$. Every such conditioning contains $d$, and $H\setminus\{d\}$ is an ample conditioning of $K$. If $H$ has $n$ active coordinates and VC dimension $k$, the minimal-nonample structure theorem gives $|H|=2\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{n-1}{i}$ and all strongly shattered sets of size at most $k-1$. Since deleting $d$ cannot create strongly shattered sets and leaves an ample class, Sauer's inequality yields $\binom{n-1}{k-1}\le1$. With $1\le k\le n-1$, this forces $k=1$, so $H$ consists of two antipodes on all its active coordinates. Restoring the fixed coordinates gives the required face.
